decisions.reason: SOL keeps the comparison’s sense while expressing it naturally.
“Dark light” preserves the ominous image without changing its meaning.
“Implied” naturally conveys what the name says.
SOL preserves the Dragon Lord’s rank, history, and realization in tighter prose.
SOL makes clear that he feels his life ending in both body and soul.
SOL preserves the thunderous sound while clarifying how he perceives it.
The surface remains clear from context; the article change does not alter the image.
SOL preserves the heart’s fragile state and the futility of stopping its cracks.
“Hasten” faithfully conveys bringing the already-foreordained destruction forward.
“Broke” preserves the physical action of breaking apart.
SOL retains both images and expresses the forbidden touch naturally.
“Gushed out” preserves the forceful image of darkness replacing blood.
SOL keeps the air trembling as if the world knows what is coming.
“Never took his eyes off” preserves the Demon Dragon’s unwavering gaze.
SOL keeps the absence of regret, anger, and cursing in natural prose.
SOL preserves the incomprehensible encouragement and its wistful cause.
The missed future amusement is preserved in H016; deleting the repeated sentence loses no meaning.
“From wherever I am” preserves the speaker’s intended meaning.
SOL preserves the Dragon’s final breath and the frozen body.
“Overflowed” reinforces the source’s image of the heart spilling its contents everywhere.
SOL preserves the paradox while making the phrasing idiomatic.
“Them both” clearly refers to darkness and brilliance, preserving the contrast.
SOL retains the pillar and the world-shaking force of the eruption.
“Feel it” preserves that Taekyung is the first and closest to experience the force.
SOL keeps the instant darkness overwhelms his vision and the lack of time to think.
“Tucked … against his chest” preserves the protective action and curled posture.
SOL preserves the wave crashing over him as it breaks the brief silence.
SOL keeps the spinning sky and earth and the full-body weightlessness.
“Fierce will” preserves his mental strength and the chime that cuts through the roar.
“Surest proof” preserves the notice as evidence of survival.
“Clinging to” keeps the image of him holding onto consciousness with all his strength.
“Hurtling” preserves the cannonball-like motion.
The collective “monster army” preserves the vast force being shattered and reduced to prey.
Naming Jin as the one who might crash preserves the subject and action.
SOL drops the explicit reference to pain; the source says he might not feel pain at all.
SOL preserves the deep sleep’s ability to make physical pain irrelevant.
SOL keeps the sense that nothing remains to prevent him from resting.
The name is not needed again; SOL carries the certainty into the next sentence.
SOL preserves the interruption just before his eyelids close.
The tense change does not alter his initial thought that he imagined the voice.
“Hear things” naturally conveys mistaking the wind for a hallucinated voice.
SOL says only that the voice itself was real, losing the source’s point that its clarity proved the whole situation was real.
“It had to be” preserves the bad-luck complaint in a natural spoken line.
SOL preserves that the gruff voice is welcome and that he forces his eyes open.
The split sentence preserves his blank stare and sudden response.
“Laughter slipped through” preserves the audible amusement in the curse.
SOL keeps the golden energy feeding on the Dragon’s overflowing magical power.
The ongoing spread of darkness is consistent with the source and preserves its sudden rush.
“Drawing it in” preserves the being’s absorption without changing the action.
SOL retains the rain, sun, and soil as forces nurturing growth.
The Korean says the golden energy becomes clearer; SOL changes that visual quality to brightness.
Removing the opening “And” does not change the growing shadow or its relation to the colors.
SOL conveys that the sight is unprecedented without changing its meaning.
SOL narrows “no ominous presence” to Jin’s perspective; the source first states it as a fact, then contrasts others’ reactions.
SOL’s version was consolidated into H054; this sentence is needed to preserve that others may condemn him but Jin will not.
“Above him” makes the crown’s position clear without changing the comparison.
“His view had stopped spinning” preserves the end of the disorientation.
SOL invents a “pair of hands”; the source only describes a familiar touch laying him down.
The unbracketed label follows the rule against square brackets for UI text.
SOL incorporates the memory of defeating the Arch Lich into the same recollection without changing its timing.
The Arch Lich memory is retained in H060, so deleting this repetition loses no content.
SOL changes the remembered words’ subject: the source says they remain clear in Jin’s memory, not that the Skeleton remembers them too.
“Burst out laughing” preserves their sudden shared laughter.
SOL keeps their uncertainty about each other’s experiences and the certainty that follows.
SOL preserves their trust and shared fight to protect what mattered to them.
The source wonders whether he has reached his limit; SOL preserves that uncertainty and the distant voice.
The italics correctly render the direct thought, and “had nothing left” preserves his exhaustion.
The italics present the repeated invitation as direct thought without changing its wording.
The Korean says his exhausted mental strength was ready to defy his own will; SOL changes the object to “him.”
“Almost before the words were out” shifts the timing earlier; the source says he fell asleep as soon as the words were finished.
SOL drops the reluctance in “차마” and the sense of one unsaid addition.
SOL preserves the ominous qualification that the rest will be too short.
The source says 정신력, or mental strength; “mind” preserves that sense better than “will.”
“Realized it himself, without being told” preserves the inference he would have made alone.
“Every bit as remarkable” preserves the comparison between his power and instincts and his temper.
“Massive” preserves the Grand Mage’s imposing size, and SOL retains his exceptional standing among humanity.
SOL keeps the confusion in both his voice and eyes.
“Entranced” preserves the dazed, spellbound way he looks around.
SOL retains the loss of both reunion’s joy and victory’s happiness.
“Forget why he was there” preserves his original purpose and its displacement by the ominous power.
“Reached such heights” preserves the mage’s advanced realm without a stiff rendering.
SOL preserves the memory of the Great Cataclysm at its height and the saturation of the surroundings.
The two sentences preserve both his involuntary tremble and realization of the cause.
SOL preserves the comparison that the Undead King’s absorbed power is negligible beside the nearly infinite source.
SOL drops the established term “magical power” for 마력; BASE preserves the chapter’s glossary rendering.
The following quote makes clear that he speaks; removing “added” does not change the action or fear.
“It’s complete” preserves the completed state in natural dialogue.
SOL retains both the final piece and the key, using a deliberate fragment for emphasis.
SOL preserves the Dragon’s death as the event that completes the beginning of another catastrophe.
SOL preserves who can hear the tone and that it reaches no one at this moment.
The streamlined phrasing preserves the prepared volcano image.
